findings.summary: A reader that lists bug-evidence will likely also write its own bug-evidence criterion, and the step will then add a second, near-identical one.
findings.evidence: reader.md:16 says 'Standing defaults like outcome-check apply unasked: record each applicable one as an acceptance criterion'. The reader sees only the first sentence of bug-evidence, so its criterion (for example 'bug-evidence: name the root cause from readable data') will not start with 'before any fix, the change states the root cause'. The step therefore adds a second criterion, which costs one more planner demonstration (admission.rs:179-197) and one more verdict item. Decision 5 handles only the overlap with the standing root-cause default. Fix: Have the step replace a criterion that starts with 'bug-evidence' with its own fuller text, or keep both, say so in §3.9, and add a test that pins the chosen behaviour.
findings.location: Decision 5 / step 6 (when to skip adding the criterion); crates/athena-context/prompts/reader.md:16

findings.summary: The keyword fallback still fires on some feature requests, such as 'Fix the bug report form', and adds a root-cause criterion that a feature job cannot meet.
findings.evidence: In 'Fix the bug report form', the fix word and the bug word have one token between them, inside the two-token window. The negative table covers 'Fix the docs for the bug report form' (four tokens between) but not this shorter case. A feature reading that gains the criterion risks the same final-verdict rejection this job is meant to stop. A more correct design is a required reader-output field (for example a yes/no 'is this bug work?') that the step enforces, which replaces word matching with the reader's own judgement. Fix: Add 'Fix the bug report form' to the tests as a pinned, known false positive, name it in the doc comment and §3.9, and record the required reader field as the follow-up alternative.

findings.summary: The retry wiring in read_once is checked only by searching source text, though a behavioural seam exists.
findings.evidence: crates/athena-cli/tests/retry.rs drives a real retry with a stand-in reader (lines 245-246 return reader output by call number), so an end-to-end retry can be run. A source-text match shows only that the argument is written, not that a retried bug job's reading gains the criterion. Fix: Add a test in retry.rs (or run/tests.rs) that retries a job whose request names a bug, with a neutral current request and title, and assert the recorded reading has the bug-evidence criterion and entry. Keep the source-text test for criterion 2.

summary: I checked the plan against the code. Every place and function it names exists: ensure_changelog at reading.rs:281; in build_reading, ensure_changelog, validate() and the empty-criteria refusal at lines 842, 843 and 844-845; build_reading's only two callers, read_once (line 642) and the test helper build_sized (line 5630); EarlierAttempt.request at briefs.rs:1991; and the test helpers reading() and defaults() in briefs.rs, which load the repo's defaults.toml. Defaults render only their first sentence into the reader prompt (defaults.rs:58-79), so a first sentence starting 'Only for…' is the right way to tell the reader the scope. The reader budget is BudgetSet::Reader at crates/athena-context/src/lib.rs:175, not in athena.toml. The only other hard-coded 2000 is the test at run_pin_tests.rs:1625, and the highest decision is D165. So the five extra files are forced, which makes Athena's minor scope findings fair; the plan already asks the user about them. The tool that would enforce the 95% headroom rule (budget-guard) is not built, so that rule is prose-only, as the plan says. No existing test request puts a bug word near a fix word, so no current integration test changes. Every criterion has a demonstration that drives real code and would fail without the change. I found three minor points: bug readings may get two near-identical root-cause criteria, the keyword fallback can still fire on some feature requests, and the retry wiring is checked only by reading source text when a behavioural test is possible. None blocks a criterion.
